subject: Archaeology
title: Thermoluminescence: Dating Pottery
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Thermoluminescence: Dating Pottery.

hook.text: When pottery is fired in a kiln, its internal radiation clock resets to zero. The clock has been ticking ever since.

buildup.text: Minerals in clay trap energy from background radiation. Heating the sample releases that energy as a faint glow.

discovery.text: The brighter the glow, the older the pottery. This technique — thermoluminescence — dates ceramics up to 100,000 years.

twist.text: It also catches fakes. Forged 'ancient' pottery glows faintly because it was fired recently.

climax.text: Thermoluminescence dated burned flints at a Neanderthal cave to 170,000 years — far older than radiocarbon can measure.

punchline.text: Pottery glows when you heat it. The older it is, the brighter it shines.

quiz.question: How does thermoluminescence detect forgeries?
options: Modern clay contains chemicals not found in ancient deposits
Recently fired pottery glows faintly because it has not accumulated much energy
The glaze on modern fakes reacts differently to ultraviolet light
